node.title: Re^2: Python 'is' command
node.author: AnomalousMonk
node.doctext:
... 'is' ... is overkill ...

I strongly agree! What's the point of bringing [metamod://Scalar::Util]::refaddr() et al to the party when == != (and all the other numeric comparators, in the unlikely event they would be of any use) seem to manage just fine: c:\@Work\Perl\monks>perl use strict; use warnings; use Test::Simple tests => 4; 1..4 sub is { $_[0] == $_[1] } my $x = 3; my $y = 3; my $x_ref = \$x; my $test_ref_1 = \$x; my $test_ref_2 = \$y; ok( is($test_ref_1, $x_ref), 'is Same' ); ok( !is($test_ref_2, $x_ref), 'is Different' ); ok( $test_ref_1 == $x_ref, '==' ); ok( $test_ref_2 != $x_ref, '!=' ); __END__ ok 1 - is Same ok 2 - is Different ok 3 - == ok 4 - !=

Give a man a fish: <%-{-{-{-<
